From b570f37a2ce480be26c665345c5514686a8a0274 Mon Sep 17 00:00:00 2001
From: =?UTF-8?q?Thomas=20Hellstr=C3=B6m?= <thomas.hellstrom@linux.intel.com>
Date: Tue, 10 Feb 2026 12:56:53 +0100
Subject: [PATCH] mm: Fix a hmm_range_fault() livelock / starvation problem
MIME-Version: 1.0
Content-Type: text/plain; charset=UTF-8
Content-Transfer-Encoding: 8bit

If hmm_range_fault() fails a folio_trylock() in do_swap_page,
trying to acquire the lock of a device-private folio for migration,
to ram, the function will spin until it succeeds grabbing the lock.

However, if the process holding the lock is depending on a work
item to be completed, which is scheduled on the same CPU as the
spinning hmm_range_fault(), that work item might be starved and
we end up in a livelock / starvation situation which is never
resolved.

This can happen, for example if the process holding the
device-private folio lock is stuck in
   migrate_device_unmap()->lru_add_drain_all()
sinc lru_add_drain_all() requires a short work-item
to be run on all online cpus to complete.

A prerequisite for this to happen is:
a) Both zone device and system memory folios are considered in
   migrate_device_unmap(), so that there is a reason to call
   lru_add_drain_all() for a system memory folio while a
   folio lock is held on a zone device folio.
b) The zone device folio has an initial mapcount > 1 which causes
   at least one migration PTE entry insertion to be deferred to
   try_to_migrate(), which can happen after the call to
   lru_add_drain_all().
c) No or voluntary only preemption.

This all seems pretty unlikely to happen, but indeed is hit by
the "xe_exec_system_allocator" igt test.

Resolve this by waiting for the folio to be unlocked if the
folio_trylock() fails in do_swap_page().

Rename migration_entry_wait_on_locked() to
softleaf_entry_wait_unlock() and update its documentation to
indicate the new use-case.

Future code improvements might consider moving
the lru_add_drain_all() call in migrate_device_unmap() to be
called *after* all pages have migration entries inserted.
That would eliminate also b) above.

v2:
- Instead of a cond_resched() in hmm_range_fault(),
  eliminate the problem by waiting for the folio to be unlocked
  in do_swap_page() (Alistair Popple, Andrew Morton)
v3:
- Add a stub migration_entry_wait_on_locked() for the
  !CONFIG_MIGRATION case. (Kernel Test Robot)
v4:
- Rename migrate_entry_wait_on_locked() to
  softleaf_entry_wait_on_locked() and update docs (Alistair Popple)
v5:
- Add a WARN_ON_ONCE() for the !CONFIG_MIGRATION
  version of softleaf_entry_wait_on_locked().
- Modify wording around function names in the commit message
  (Andrew Morton)

Suggested-by: Alistair Popple <apopple@nvidia.com>
Fixes: 1afaeb8293c9 ("mm/migrate: Trylock device page in do_swap_page")
Cc: Ralph Campbell <rcampbell@nvidia.com>
Cc: Christoph Hellwig <hch@lst.de>
Cc: Jason Gunthorpe <jgg@mellanox.com>

(cherry picked from commit a69d1ab971a624c6f112cea61536569d579c3215)
Signed-off-by: Rodrigo Vivi <rodrigo.vivi@intel.com>

diff --git a/mm/migrate_device.c b/mm/migrate_device.c
index 0a8b31939640..8079676c8f1f 100644
--- a/mm/migrate_device.c
+++ b/mm/migrate_device.c
@@ -176,7 +176,7 @@ static int migrate_vma_collect_huge_pmd(pmd_t *pmdp, unsigned long start,
 		}
 
 		if (softleaf_is_migration(entry)) {
-			migration_entry_wait_on_locked(entry, ptl);
+			softleaf_entry_wait_on_locked(entry, ptl);
 			spin_unlock(ptl);
 			return -EAGAIN;
 		}
-- 
2.34.1



diff --git a/include/linux/migrate.h b/include/linux/migrate.h
index 26ca00c325d9..d5af2b7f577b 100644
--- a/include/linux/migrate.h
+++ b/include/linux/migrate.h
@@ -65,7 +65,7 @@ bool isolate_folio_to_list(struct folio *folio, struct list_head *list);
 
 int migrate_huge_page_move_mapping(struct address_space *mapping,
 		struct folio *dst, struct folio *src);
-void migration_entry_wait_on_locked(softleaf_t entry, spinlock_t *ptl)
+void softleaf_entry_wait_on_locked(softleaf_t entry, spinlock_t *ptl)
 		__releases(ptl);
 void folio_migrate_flags(struct folio *newfolio, struct folio *folio);
 int folio_migrate_mapping(struct address_space *mapping,
@@ -97,6 +97,14 @@ static inline int set_movable_ops(const struct movable_operations *ops, enum pag
 	return -ENOSYS;
 }
 
+static inline void softleaf_entry_wait_on_locked(softleaf_t entry, spinlock_t *ptl)
+	__releases(ptl)
+{
+	WARN_ON_ONCE(1);
+
+	spin_unlock(ptl);
+}
+
 #endif /* CONFIG_MIGRATION */
 
 #ifdef CONFIG_NUMA_BALANCING

diff --git a/mm/migrate.c b/mm/migrate.c
index 1bf2cf8c44dd..2c3d489ecf51 100644
--- a/mm/migrate.c
+++ b/mm/migrate.c
@@ -500,7 +500,7 @@ void migration_entry_wait(struct mm_struct *mm, pmd_t *pmd,
 	if (!softleaf_is_migration(entry))
 		goto out;
 
-	migration_entry_wait_on_locked(entry, ptl);
+	softleaf_entry_wait_on_locked(entry, ptl);
 	return;
 out:
 	spin_unlock(ptl);
@@ -532,10 +532,10 @@ void migration_entry_wait_huge(struct vm_area_struct *vma, unsigned long addr, p
 		 * If migration entry existed, safe to release vma lock
 		 * here because the pgtable page won't be freed without the
 		 * pgtable lock released.  See comment right above pgtable
-		 * lock release in migration_entry_wait_on_locked().
+		 * lock release in softleaf_entry_wait_on_locked().
 		 */
 		hugetlb_vma_unlock_read(vma);
-		migration_entry_wait_on_locked(entry, ptl);
+		softleaf_entry_wait_on_locked(entry, ptl);
 		return;
 	}
 
@@ -553,7 +553,7 @@ void pmd_migration_entry_wait(struct mm_struct *mm, pmd_t *pmd)
 	ptl = pmd_lock(mm, pmd);
 	if (!pmd_is_migration_entry(*pmd))
 		goto unlock;
-	migration_entry_wait_on_locked(softleaf_from_pmd(*pmd), ptl);
+	softleaf_entry_wait_on_locked(softleaf_from_pmd(*pmd), ptl);
 	return;
 unlock:
 	spin_unlock(ptl);

diff --git a/mm/filemap.c b/mm/filemap.c
index 6cd7974d4ada..406cef06b684 100644
--- a/mm/filemap.c
+++ b/mm/filemap.c
@@ -1379,14 +1379,16 @@ static inline int folio_wait_bit_common(struct folio *folio, int bit_nr,
 
 #ifdef CONFIG_MIGRATION
 /**
- * migration_entry_wait_on_locked - Wait for a migration entry to be removed
- * @entry: migration swap entry.
+ * softleaf_entry_wait_on_locked - Wait for a migration entry or
+ * device_private entry to be removed.
+ * @entry: migration or device_private swap entry.
  * @ptl: already locked ptl. This function will drop the lock.
  *
- * Wait for a migration entry referencing the given page to be removed. This is
+ * Wait for a migration entry referencing the given page, or device_private
+ * entry referencing a dvice_private page to be unlocked. This is
  * equivalent to folio_put_wait_locked(folio, TASK_UNINTERRUPTIBLE) except
  * this can be called without taking a reference on the page. Instead this
- * should be called while holding the ptl for the migration entry referencing
+ * should be called while holding the ptl for @entry referencing
  * the page.
  *
  * Returns after unlocking the ptl.
@@ -1394,7 +1396,7 @@ static inline int folio_wait_bit_common(struct folio *folio, int bit_nr,
  * This follows the same logic as folio_wait_bit_common() so see the comments
  * there.
  */
-void migration_entry_wait_on_locked(softleaf_t entry, spinlock_t *ptl)
+void softleaf_entry_wait_on_locked(softleaf_t entry, spinlock_t *ptl)
 	__releases(ptl)
 {
 	struct wait_page_queue wait_page;
@@ -1428,6 +1430,9 @@ void migration_entry_wait_on_locked(softleaf_t entry, spinlock_t *ptl)
 	 * If a migration entry exists for the page the migration path must hold
 	 * a valid reference to the page, and it must take the ptl to remove the
 	 * migration entry. So the page is valid until the ptl is dropped.
+	 * Similarly any path attempting to drop the last reference to a
+	 * device-private page needs to grab the ptl to remove the device-private
+	 * entry.
 	 */
 	spin_unlock(ptl);
 

diff --git a/mm/memory.c b/mm/memory.c
index 07778814b4a8..2f815a34d924 100644
--- a/mm/memory.c
+++ b/mm/memory.c
@@ -4763,7 +4763,8 @@ vm_fault_t do_swap_page(struct vm_fault *vmf)
 				unlock_page(vmf->page);
 				put_page(vmf->page);
 			} else {
-				pte_unmap_unlock(vmf->pte, vmf->ptl);
+				pte_unmap(vmf->pte);
+				softleaf_entry_wait_on_locked(entry, vmf->ptl);
 			}
 		} else if (softleaf_is_hwpoison(entry)) {
 			ret = VM_FAULT_HWPOISON;

## Summary of Modifications

### Modifications in Each File

1. **include/linux/migrate.h**  
   - Renamed `migration_entry_wait_on_locked()` to `softleaf_entry_wait_on_locked()`.  
   - Added a stub for the `!CONFIG_MIGRATION` case, which includes a `WARN_ON_ONCE(1)` and simply releases the PTL spinlock.

2. **mm/migrate_device.c**  
   - Updated one call site from `migration_entry_wait_on_locked()` to `softleaf_entry_wait_on_locked()`.

3. **mm/migrate.c**  
   - Updated three call sites (`migration_entry_wait`, `migration_entry_wait_huge`, `pmd_migration_entry_wait`) from `migration_entry_wait_on_locked()` to `softleaf_entry_wait_on_locked()`.  
   - Adjusted a code comment to reference the new function name.

4. **mm/filemap.c**  
   - Renamed the function `migration_entry_wait_on_locked()` to `softleaf_entry_wait_on_locked()`.  
   - Expanded its documentation to clarify that it now handles both migration entries **and** device-private entries, waiting for the associated folio to become unlocked.  
   - Added a comment explaining that the last reference to a device-private page also needs to hold the PTL when removing the entry.

5. **mm/memory.c**  
   - In `do_swap_page()`, when `folio_trylock()` fails for a device-private folio (i.e., the folio is locked by another process), the code no longer simply releases the PTL and returns. Instead, it unmaps the PTE, then calls `softleaf_entry_wait_on_locked()` to wait for the folio to be unlocked, before releasing the PTL.

### Relationships Among the Changes

The core fix targets a livelock/starvation in `hmm_range_fault()`. The problem occurred when `do_swap_page()` encountered a device-private folio that was locked by another process (e.g., inside `migrate_device_unmap()`). Previously, the code would busy-wait by retrying `folio_trylock()` on every re-entry into `do_swap_page()`, starving a work‑item scheduled on the same CPU.

The solution changes the behavior: instead of spinning, the fault handler now **waits** until the folio is unlocked. This is achieved by calling the existing waiting mechanism (`softleaf_entry_wait_on_locked`), which was originally designed only for migration entries. The patch renames this function to reflect its broader applicability (both migration and device‑private entries) and updates all call sites across `mm/migrate.c`, `mm/migrate_device.c`, and `mm/memory.c`. Additionally, the documentation in `mm/filemap.c` is updated to describe the new use case, and a stub is added for configurations without `CONFIG_MIGRATION`.

The changes are interdependent: the rename in `include/linux/migrate.h` and `mm/filemap.c` provides the generalized API, while the modification in `mm/memory.c` is the actual fix. The updates in `mm/migrate.c` and `mm/migrate_device.c` are mechanical callsite updates to match the rename.

## Summary of Modifications

This patch fixes a livelock/starvation bug in `hmm_range_fault()` when a `folio_trylock()` fails in `do_swap_page()` for a device-private folio. The root cause is that the spinning loop never yields, causing a CPU-bound process to starve a work item needed to release the lock. The fix replaces the spin with a proper wait, and renames the associated wait function to reflect the broader use case (now also covering device-private entries).

### Modifications in Each File

1. **mm/memory.c** (`do_swap_page`):
   - Replaced the unconditional spin (via `pte_unmap_unlock`) with a call to `softleaf_entry_wait_on_locked()` after unmapping the PTE. This waits for the folio to be unlocked instead of busy-waiting.

2. **mm/filemap.c** (definition of the wait function):
   - Renamed `migration_entry_wait_on_locked()` to `softleaf_entry_wait_on_locked()`.
   - Updated the docstring to indicate it now handles both migration and device-private entries.

3. **include/linux/migrate.h** (declaration and stub):

### Relationships Between Modifications

From b570f37a2ce480be26c665345c5514686a8a0274 Mon Sep 17 00:00:00 2001
From: =?UTF-8?q?Thomas=20Hellstr=C3=B6m?= <thomas.hellstrom@linux.intel.com>
Date: Tue, 10 Feb 2026 12:56:53 +0100
Subject: [PATCH] mm: Fix a hmm_range_fault() livelock / starvation problem
MIME-Version: 1.0
Content-Type: text/plain; charset=UTF-8
Content-Transfer-Encoding: 8bit

If hmm_range_fault() fails a folio_trylock() in do_swap_page,
trying to acquire the lock of a device-private folio for migration,
to ram, the function will spin until it succeeds grabbing the lock.

However, if the process holding the lock is depending on a work
item to be completed, which is scheduled on the same CPU as the
spinning hmm_range_fault(), that work item might be starved and
we end up in a livelock / starvation situation which is never
resolved.

This can happen, for example if the process holding the
device-private folio lock is stuck in
   migrate_device_unmap()->lru_add_drain_all()
sinc lru_add_drain_all() requires a short work-item
to be run on all online cpus to complete.

A prerequisite for this to happen is:
a) Both zone device and system memory folios are considered in
   migrate_device_unmap(), so that there is a reason to call
   lru_add_drain_all() for a system memory folio while a
   folio lock is held on a zone device folio.
b) The zone device folio has an initial mapcount > 1 which causes
   at least one migration PTE entry insertion to be deferred to
   try_to_migrate(), which can happen after the call to
   lru_add_drain_all().
c) No or voluntary only preemption.

This all seems pretty unlikely to happen, but indeed is hit by
the "xe_exec_system_allocator" igt test.

Resolve this by waiting for the folio to be unlocked if the
folio_trylock() fails in do_swap_page().

Rename migration_entry_wait_on_locked() to
softleaf_entry_wait_unlock() and update its documentation to
indicate the new use-case.

Future code improvements might consider moving
the lru_add_drain_all() call in migrate_device_unmap() to be
called *after* all pages have migration entries inserted.
That would eliminate also b) above.

v2:
- Instead of a cond_resched() in hmm_range_fault(),
  eliminate the problem by waiting for the folio to be unlocked
  in do_swap_page() (Alistair Popple, Andrew Morton)
v3:
- Add a stub migration_entry_wait_on_locked() for the
  !CONFIG_MIGRATION case. (Kernel Test Robot)
v4:
- Rename migrate_entry_wait_on_locked() to
  softleaf_entry_wait_on_locked() and update docs (Alistair Popple)
v5:
- Add a WARN_ON_ONCE() for the !CONFIG_MIGRATION
  version of softleaf_entry_wait_on_locked().
- Modify wording around function names in the commit message
  (Andrew Morton)

+void softleaf_entry_wait_on_locked(softleaf_t entry, spinlock_t *ptl)
 	__releases(ptl)
 {
 	struct wait_page_queue wait_page;
@@ -1428,6 +1430,9 @@ void migration_entry_wait_on_locked(softleaf_t entry, spinlock_t *ptl)
 	 * If a migration entry exists for the page the migration path must hold

 	 * migration entry. So the page is valid until the ptl is dropped.
+	 * Similarly any path attempting to drop the last reference to a
+	 * device-private page needs to grab the ptl to remove the device-private
+	 * entry.
 	 */
 	spin_unlock(ptl);

## Summary of Modifications

This patch fixes a livelock/starvation issue in `hmm_range_fault()` when a CPU-bound thread unable to acquire the lock of a device-private folio in `do_swap_page()`. The previous code would spin indefinitely on `folio_trylock()`, but if the lock holder requires a work item scheduled on the same CPU (e.g., via `lru_add_drain_all()`), the spinner can starve it, causing deadlock.

The fix replaces the spin-wait with a proper wait-for-unlock mechanism, using an existing function that already waits for migration entries to be removed. To reflect its new role, the function is renamed and its documentation updated.

### Modifications in Each File

1. **`mm/filemap.c`**  
   - Renamed `migration_entry_wait_on_locked()` to `softleaf_entry_wait_on_locked()`.  
   - Updated its documentation to explicitly state that it now also waits for device-private swap entries (not only migration entries) to be unlocked.

2. **`mm/migrate.c`**  
   - Updated three call sites (`migration_entry_wait`, `migration_entry_wait_huge`, `pmd_migration_entry_wait`) to call the new name `softleaf_entry_wait_on_locked` instead of the old name.

3. **`include/linux/migrate.h`**  
   - Updated the declaration of the function to the new name.  
   - Added a stub implementation for `!CONFIG_MIGRATION` that issues a `WARN_ON_ONCE` and releases the ptl lock (to avoid compilation errors).

4. **`mm/migrate_device.c`**  
   - Updated a call site (`migrate_vma_collect_huge_pmd`) to use the new function name.

5. **`mm/memory.c`** (most important functional change)  
   - In `do_swap_page()`, when handling a device-private swap entry and `folio_trylock()` fails, the old code just unlocked and put the page.  
   - The new code unmaps the PTE (`pte_unmap`) and then calls `softleaf_entry_wait_on_locked()` to wait until the folio is unlocked, then the function continues (the ptl is released by the wait function). This prevents spinning and allows the lock holder to make progress.

### Relationships Between Changes

- **Renaming and documentation** (`filemap.c`, `migrate.c`, `include/linux/migrate.h`, `migrate_device.c`) are purely mechanical but necessary to support the new use case (device‑private entries) without confusion.  
- **The stub in `migrate.h`** ensures the new usage in `memory.c` compiles even when `CONFIG_MIGRATION` is disabled, by providing a safe fallback.  
- **The core fix** is in `memory.c`: the call to `softleaf_entry_wait_on_locked()` replaces the previous spin‑wait on `folio_trylock()`. This function already had the right logic to wait for a page to be unlocked (used for migration entries), and the rename clarifies that it is also suitable for device‑private entries.  
- All other file changes are simply updates to use the renamed function, maintaining consistency across the migration‑related code paths.

In summary, the patch re‑purposes an existing wait mechanism for migration entries to also cover device‑private folio locks, thereby eliminating the busy‑spin that caused the livelock.
